title: Buddhism: the man under the tree
hookLine: Siddhartha leaves a palace, sits under a tree at Bodh Gaya, and wakes up

lines: A PALACE, AND A FATHER'S PLAN.
OLD AGE, SICKNESS, DEATH, A MONK.
cards: A palace. A beautiful family, servants, music, a future as king, and a father determined that his son will never see anything sad. Then one day the son sees it anyway.
Old age. Sickness. A body being carried to be burned.
And a wandering holy man, calm in the middle of it all. It can't be unseen.
In the story Buddhists tell, that's how a young prince named Siddhartha Gautama walked out of his palace one night and went looking for a way through.

teach.b: Siddhartha was born in Lumbini, in what's now southern Nepal, into the Shakya clan, in a century scholars still debate.
The four sights, the old man, the sick man, the corpse and the monk, come from later biographies, and Buddhists treasure them as the heart of why he left.
As a young man he left home, and for years he tried what the holy men of his day taught, including fasting so hard, the texts say, that he could feel his spine through his stomach. It didn't work.
So he did something his companions thought was giving up: he ate. A bowl of rice and milk, offered, in the traditional story, by a young woman named Sujata.
Then he sat down under a tree at a place now called Bodh Gaya, in northern India, and resolved not to get up until he understood.

The tradition says Mara, the tempter, came with fear and desire and doubt, and that Siddhartha touched the earth as his witness. Through the night he saw clearly, and by dawn, Buddhists say, he had woken up.
That's the name: the word Buddha is formed from a root meaning to wake.

teach.h: A BOWL OF RICE, THEN THE TREE.
teach.b: The Buddha is the awakened one, and the tree became the Bodhi tree, the tree of awakening.
Buddhists honor him not as a creator god but as a teacher who found the way and showed it.
The texts even say he hesitated to teach at first, thinking no one would understand. Then he got up and walked to find his old companions.

how: Buddhists around the world tell the story of the Buddha's leaving home and awakening, and many make pilgrimage to Bodh Gaya, where a descendant of the Bodhi tree still grows beside the Mahabodhi Temple.

o: the path taught by the Buddha, the one who woke up
a way of life built mostly around long, hard fasting
the worship of a smiling god who brings good fortune

p: offered the bowl of rice and milk
where he sat under the tree

s: Buddhists worship the Buddha as the creator god
Buddhists honor him as a teacher who found the way and showed it.
Siddhartha found awakening by starving himself
years of harsh fasting didn't work; he ate, then sat under the tree.
Buddha comes from a root meaning to wake

games.q: you've just woken up under the tree. you understand something deep, and it's subtle and hard to say. what do you do?
o: keep it to yourself; nobody will get it.
write it down and stay under the tree forever.
games.why: the texts say the Buddha first hesitated, thinking no one would understand. then he got up and walked to find his old companions, and began to teach.

practice: If you're near a tree, sit with your back to it; if not, picture a wide, shady tree above you, its leaves moving. Rest a hand on something solid: the ground, the floor, your knee.
Then just be awake to what's here, the sounds, the air, your breathing, with nothing to become.

wordCard.voice: Buddhism. The path of the Buddha, the awakened one: a prince who left his palace, sat under a tree at Bodh Gaya, and woke up. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali and Sanskrit: awakened, from the root budh, to wake.

carryVoice: Your line: wake up. Tomorrow, the first thing he taught. Day two hundred thirty-nine, done.
